fitness.read: The blue line (fitness) rises when you train consistently and slowly falls when you rest. The pink one (fatigue) reacts quickly to each session. Grey bars are each day's load.
fitness.good: Fitness rising gently week after week.
fitness.watch: Fatigue staying well above fitness: you are piling on more than you absorb.

tsb.read: Freshness = fitness − fatigue. Below 0 you are loading up; above 0 you are recovering.
tsb.good: Between −10 and −30 during training blocks (green zone), above +5 before a race.
tsb.watch: Below −30 (red zone) for several days: risk of overreaching.

acwr.read: Compares this week's load with the last 6 weeks. 1 = same load as usual.
acwr.good: Staying within the green band (0.8 to 1.3): steady progress.
acwr.watch: Above 1.5: a sudden jump, injury risk rises sharply.

loadBySport.read: Each bar stacks the week's load by sport. Walking and hiking only partly count, as in the fitness model.
loadBySport.watch: A big week in an unusual sport is more tiring than it looks.

projection.read: Dashed: what your fitness and freshness will become if you follow your plan to the letter.
projection.good: Positive freshness on race day: you arrive rested with fitness at its peak.
projection.watch: Very negative freshness on race day: the taper may be too short.

adherence.read: Grey bars: duration planned by your plan. Green bars: duration actually done.
adherence.good: Completing most of the volume, especially key sessions.
adherence.watch: Doing much more than planned: the plan is calibrated so you progress without injury.

calendar.read: One square per day, darker with more load. Click a square to open the session.
calendar.good: Squares spread evenly, with light recovery days.
calendar.watch: Long grey stretches (breaks) or all-dark weeks without rest.

volume.read: Volume per week or month, stacked by sport. Distance shows sport by sport: a swum kilometre is not a run kilometre.
volume.good: At most 10 % more from one week to the next, with a lighter week every 3 to 4 weeks.
volume.watch: A sudden jump in volume after a quiet period.

regularity.read: How many sessions you do on each day of the week over the period.
regularity.good: Stable training days: habit is your best ally.

intensity.read: Bars show time in each heart rate zone. The black line shows the share of easy endurance (Z1–Z2).
intensity.good: About 80 % of time in Z1–Z2 (above the dashed line) and the rest at genuine intensity (Z4–Z5).
intensity.watch: Lots of Z3: this grey zone is tiring without really building endurance or speed.

records.read: Your best time over each distance, measured inside any session (not only races).
records.good: Period records close to your all-time bests: you are in shape.

paceCurve.read: The average pace of your records, from shortest to longest distance. Higher = faster.
paceCurve.good: A gently sloping curve: your endurance keeps up with your speed.
paceCurve.watch: A sharp drop on long distances: endurance is the thing to work on.

predictions.read: Two methods: VDOT (Jack Daniels' tables, from your best efforts) and Riegel (extrapolation of a single effort).
predictions.watch: For half marathon and marathon, predictions assume specific endurance training: they are often optimistic.

vdotHistory.read: Your VDOT computed month by month from your best efforts.
vdotHistory.good: One point up ≈ 1 to 2 % faster over every distance.

ef.read: Speed divided by heart rate, on easy runs only. Higher means faster for the same effort.
ef.good: A line rising over several weeks.
ef.watch: A lasting drop: fatigue, heat or lack of base endurance.

decoupling.read: On runs over one hour: how much your heart rate climbs in the second half at the same pace.
decoupling.good: Under 5 % (green bars): your endurance base holds up.
decoupling.watch: Above 5 % (yellow bars): base endurance still needs work.

hrAtPace.read: Your average heart rate, month by month, on runs at the reference pace.
hrAtPace.good: Heart rate dropping at the same pace: your heart works less for the same effort.

hrv.read: Heart rate variability measured overnight. The blue band is your personal normal (average of the last 60 days).
hrv.good: A 7-day average within or above your normal band.
hrv.watch: Several days below your band: incomplete recovery, stress or oncoming illness.

restingHr.read: Your resting heart rate, day by day and as a 7-day average.
restingHr.good: Stable or slowly decreasing over the months.
restingHr.watch: More than 5 bpm above usual: fatigue or illness.

sleep.read: Length of each night, split by stage when your watch provides it.
sleep.good: 7 to 9 h a night, more during big weeks.

loadVsHrv.read: Bars: previous day's load. Line: morning HRV. A big day normally lowers HRV the next morning.
loadVsHrv.good: HRV bouncing back within 1 to 2 days after a hard session.
loadVsHrv.watch: HRV staying low despite easy days.

correlation.read: Each dot is a session: sleep the night before and the session's efficiency. r measures the link (from −1 to 1).
correlation.good: r > 0.3: for you, better sleep shows in your sessions.
correlation.watch: Correlation is not causation: many points are needed to conclude.

swimPace.read: Your average pace per 100 m, week by week. Higher = faster. The CSS line is your threshold pace.
swimPace.good: A pace getting closer to your CSS on long sessions.

watchScores.read: The scores your watch computes every day (out of 100). Each brand has its own recipe: follow the trend rather than the absolute value.
watchScores.good: Scores that stay stable or rise during heavy weeks.
watchScores.watch: Several low days in a row, especially alongside a low HRV.

sleepSchedule.read: Each bar runs from bedtime (top) to wake-up time (bottom).
sleepSchedule.good: Aligned bars: regular hours help your body recover.
sleepSchedule.watch: Hours varying by more than an hour from one night to the next.

hrr.read: How many beats your heart rate drops in the minute after an effort. Higher means your heart recovers faster.
hrr.good: More than 20 bpm, and a value rising over the months.
hrr.watch: A clear drop compared with usual: accumulated fatigue.

insights.fitnessRising: Your fitness is improving: {delta} over 4 weeks. Your training is paying off.
insights.fitnessFalling: Your fitness is dropping: {delta} over 4 weeks. Normal after a break or a taper; otherwise build back up gradually.
insights.fitnessStable: Your fitness is stable around {ctl}: you are maintaining your level.
insights.rampTooFast: Your fitness is rising very fast (+{ramp} in 7 days): above +8, injury risk increases. Ease off a little.
insights.overreached: Freshness at {tsb}: you are piling up fatigue. Plan a few easy days.
insights.productive: Freshness at {tsb}: productive zone, you are loading up without overdoing it.
insights.fresh: Freshness at +{tsb}: you are rested, a good time for a key session or a race.
insights.balanced: Freshness at {tsb}: load and recovery are balanced.
insights.acwrDanger: This week's load is {acwr} times your usual: a sudden jump, high injury risk.
insights.acwrHigh: This week's load is {acwr} times your usual: a marked increase, listen to your body.
insights.acwrLow: Your recent load is below your usual ({acwr}): recovery or slowing down?
insights.monotonyHigh: Very monotonous week (monotony {monotony}): alternate hard and easy days.
insights.volumeUp: Volume up {percent} % compared with the comparison period.
insights.volumeDown: Volume down {percent} % compared with the comparison period.
insights.volumeSteady: Volume stable compared with the comparison period ({percent} %).
insights.streak: {weeks} active weeks in a row: consistency is your best ally.
insights.irregular: {active} active weeks out of {weeks}: more consistency would help you progress.
insights.polarized: {percent} % of time in easy endurance (Z1–Z2) over 4 weeks: good distribution.
insights.tooGrey: Only {percent} % of time in easy endurance (Z1–Z2) over 4 weeks: slow down your easy runs (guideline: 80 %).
insights.efficiencyUp: Your aerobic efficiency is up {percent} %: you go faster for the same heart rate.
insights.efficiencyDown: Your aerobic efficiency is down {percent} %: fatigue, heat or lack of endurance?
insights.decouplingGood: {percent} % cardiac drift on your long runs: your endurance base is solid.
insights.decouplingHigh: {percent} % cardiac drift on your long runs: base endurance still needs work (guideline: < 5 %).
insights.newRecord: New record over {distance}: {time} ({count} record(s) broken in the period).
insights.vdotUp: Your VDOT went from {from} to {to}: you are faster over every distance.
insights.vdotDown: Your VDOT went from {from} to {to} over the period.
insights.goalOnTrack: Goal within reach: your prediction is {gap} under your target time.
insights.goalGap: {gap} still to gain to reach your goal.
insights.raceDayTired: With your plan you would arrive tired on race day (freshness {tsb}): consider a lighter final week.
insights.hrvLow: HRV below your normal for {days} days: consider easing off.
insights.readinessLow: Low readiness today: favour an easy session or rest.
insights.readinessGood: Good readiness today: your body has recovered well.
insights.swimFaster: Your swim pace improved by {percent} % over the period.
insights.swimSlower: Your swim pace slowed by {percent} % over the period.
insights.sleepShort: You sleep {minutes} on average over the last 2 weeks: under 7 h, your recovery suffers.
insights.bedtimeIrregular: Your bedtime varies by ± {minutes}: more regular hours improve recovery.
insights.hrrUp: Your heart rate drops faster after effort ({delta} bpm in 1 min): your cardio fitness is improving.
insights.hrrDown: Your heart rate drops more slowly after effort ({delta} bpm in 1 min): possible fatigue.
